name: MyNewTerm
description: Schools and multi-academy trusts in England post a job, and the candidate applies once instead of filling in a Word form for every school. A former maths teacher built it after doing those forms himself.

mentions.evidence: Company-stated, Practical Founders, July 2026. Surpassed £5M in revenue. 20 employees. More than 6,000 schools and 500 multi-academy trusts. More than 100,000 applications a month. About 45% of multi-academy trusts, against a private-equity incumbent. No funding round. A £5,000 innovation voucher, and the founder put more than £100K of personal debt in.
mentions.indieAngle: One country, one public employer, the application the school already has to collect.

whyItPrints: It is a hiring form for a sector that was still on Word. Once a trust runs hiring through it, switching is painful. The two-sided start was the hard part.
whyThisMatters:
A teacher applying for a job in England used to fill in a Word form for every school. MyNewTerm is the marketplace and the tracking system instead. Schools and multi-academy trusts post the vacancy. The candidate applies once. A former maths teacher built it, and he also referees football.

The company says revenue is past five million pounds, with twenty people, thousands of schools, and about half of the multi-academy trusts. There was no funding round. There was a small innovation voucher, and the founder put a lot of his own debt in. That is a July 2026 interview. It is not a Stripe connection.

You pay so the application is one form, not a stack of Word files.

More than six thousand schools and five hundred trusts are the footprint. A hundred thousand applications a month is the volume. About forty-five percent of multi-academy trusts is the share he claims, against a private-equity incumbent. The five-thousand-pound voucher and more than a hundred thousand of personal debt are the funding story. Twenty employees.
